title: Build objects from compact generators by a homotopy colimit
statement: Let C be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with set-indexed coproducts and a set (E_i) of compact objects [def-pc-compact-object] whose coproduct is a generator [def-pc-generators]. Every object Y of C is a sequential homotopy colimit of a sequence X_1 \to X_2 \to \cdots, that is, there is a distinguished triangle \bigoplus_n X_n \xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}} \bigoplus_n X_n \to Y \to (\bigoplus_n X_n)[1], where X_1 is a coproduct of shifts of the E_i and each transition X_n \to X_{n+1} fits into a distinguished triangle Z_n \to X_n \to X_{n+1} \to Z_n[1], where Z_n is a coproduct of shifts of the E_i.

proof.text: Fix an object Y of C. Let X_1=\bigoplus_{(i,m,\varphi)} E_i[m], the coproduct indexed by all triples (i,m,\varphi) with i in the indexing set, m\in\mathbf Z and \varphi:E_i[m]\to Y. The maps \varphi assemble, by the universal property of the coproduct, to a canonical morphism X_1\to Y, and X_1 has the required form by construction.

source.place: Tag 09SN, Lemma lemma-write-as-colimit, proof: construction of X_1

proof.text: Inductively, suppose a morphism f_n:X_n\to Y has been constructed. Let Z_n=\bigoplus_{(i,m,\varphi)} E_i[m], indexed by the triples (i,m,\varphi) with \varphi:E_i[m]\to X_n and f_n\circ\varphi=0, and let u_n:Z_n\to X_n be the map assembled from the \varphi. Complete u_n to a distinguished triangle Z_n\xrightarrow{u_n}X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]. Since f_n\circ u_n=0 (it vanishes on every summand), exactness of \Hom(-,Y) on this triangle gives f_{n+1}:X_{n+1}\to Y whose composite with X_n\to X_{n+1} is f_n. Thus every transition has the asserted triangle and Z_n is a coproduct of shifts of the E_i.

source.place: Tag 09SN, Lemma lemma-write-as-colimit, proof: inductive construction of Y_n and X_{n+1}

proof.text: Form the telescope X of the sequence by a distinguished triangle \bigoplus_n X_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\bigoplus_n X_n\to X\to(\bigoplus_n X_n)[1]. The map (f_n)_n:\bigoplus_n X_n\to Y vanishes after composing with 1-\mathrm{shift}, because the f_n commute with the transition maps; exactness of \Hom(-,Y) on the telescope triangle gives f:X\to Y restricting to f_n on each X_n. Complete f to a distinguished triangle C\to X\xrightarrow{f}Y\to C[1] and rotate it to Y[-1]\to C\to X\to Y. Compactness is invariant under shifts (the shift is an automorphism commuting with coproducts, so the defining coproduct bijection for E_i applies to E_i[m]). Let \alpha:E_i[m]\to C. By the compact-Hom homotopy-colimit lemma, the composite E_i[m]\to C\to X equals E_i[m]\xrightarrow{\beta}X_n\to X for some n and \beta. Then f_n\circ\beta=f\circ(E_i[m]\to C\to X)=0, since C\to X\to Y is zero, so \beta is a summand index of Z_n and E_i[m]\xrightarrow{\beta}X_n\to X_{n+1} is zero; as X_n\to X factors through X_{n+1}\to X, the composite E_i[m]\to C\to X is zero. Exactness of \Hom(E_i[m],-) on the rotated triangle gives \gamma:E_i[m]\to Y[-1] with \alpha equal to \gamma followed by Y[-1]\to C. The shift \gamma[1]:E_i[m+1]\to Y is a summand index of X_1, so \gamma[1] factors through X_1\to X\xrightarrow{f}Y, hence \gamma factors through f[-1]:X[-1]\to Y[-1]; since X[-1]\to Y[-1]\to C is a composite of consecutive maps of a distinguished triangle, it is zero, and \alpha=0. So every map from every E_i[m] to C is zero; hence every map \bigoplus_i E_i\to C[n] is zero, and since \bigoplus_i E_i is a generator, C=0. Then f is an isomorphism (exactness of \Hom(W,-) on the triangle with C=0), and replacing X by Y through f in the telescope triangle gives a distinguished triangle by (TR1), so Y is the asserted sequential homotopy colimit.

source.place: Tag 09SN, Lemma lemma-write-as-colimit, proof: telescope triangle and vanishing of its cone
